# DSH 0.1.5 → 0.1.7 plugin settings migration English | [中文](SETTINGS-MIGRATION.zh-CN.md) This collects every settings-page difference we hit while migrating from DSH 0.1.5 to 0.1.7, each with the verbatim error we measured. You can forward it to other plugin authors as-is. ## In one line **0.1.7 removed `settings.register()`.** On 0.1.5 a plugin could open a settings namespace **by name**. On 0.1.7, the namespace *is* a profile entry id, and the schema *is* that entry's Config. The migration is therefore not an API change but a change to **the plugin's identity in the profile**. ## Side by side | | 0.1.5 and earlier | 0.1.7 | |---|---|---| | Where the namespace comes from | the plugin calls `settings.register('my-plugin', schema)` | the profile entry id (the `- id: …` row in [`cordis.patch.yml`](../cordis.patch.yml)) | | Where the schema comes from | passed at registration | the entry's `config` field, validated by the host against the plugin's exported `Config` | | How the client reads and writes | the api-proxy settings channel | the same, except the **namespace must be in the host's list** | ## Three traps, in the order we hit them ### Trap 1: `settings.register` is no longer a function **Symptom**, in the startup log. Without a guard, the plugin fails to load: ``` [modsearch] settings namespace skipped: TypeError: scope.settings.register is not a function ``` **Fix**: stop calling it. Export the schema as the plugin's `Config` and read and write through the host settings service by **entry id**. ### Trap 2: the entry id carries a **kind prefix**, the settings service only knows the **bare id** This is the worst one, because the error gives no hint of the real cause: ``` POST /my-plugin/prefs 409 settings-conflict No configurable plugin entry "include:ui-skin-claude-style" ``` **Root cause**: the 0.1.7 loader reports the entry id as **`:`**. A plugin in a profile is usually an **`include` or `insert` entry**, so `ctx.fiber.entry.id` yields `include:ui-skin-claude-style`. The **settings service indexes namespaces by the bare id**, though: its list literally contains `ui-skin-claude-style`. Write with the prefixed name and the host cannot find the entry, so **every save returns 409**. **Fix**, one line: ```js // 0.1.7 reports ":"; the settings service wants the bare id; no-op without a prefix function entryIdOf(ctx) { const id = ctx?.fiber?.entry?.id if (typeof id === 'string' && id !== '') { const colon = id.lastIndexOf(':') return colon === -1 ? id : id.slice(colon + 1) } return ENTRY_ID_FALLBACK // the id declared in the patch } ``` **Measured**: before the fix, `namespaceState = configured:include:ui-skin-claude-style` and writes returned 409. After it, `configured:ui-skin-claude-style` and writes return `200 {"ok":true,…,"revision":1,"available":true}`. ### Trap 3: `schemastery` does not resolve from the plugin's own location **Symptom**: Config validation cannot get the schema, so the namespace never registers. Reads survive on defaults, but writes always fail. **Cause**: plugins are often installed into a profile as a **symlink or local link**, and there is no `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` under its own `require` anchor. **Fix**: point the resolution anchor at the **running harness bin**, which always ships schemastery, and fall back to normal resolution afterwards: ```js import { createRequire } from 'node:module' import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url' const anchor = pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href // e.g. /@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js const factory = createRequire(anchor)('@deepseek-ai/schemastery') // on failure, await import('@deepseek-ai/schemastery') ``` There is also a **load-time** trap. `.volatile()` only exists on 0.1.7; an older host ships a schemastery without it. Building a volatile `Config` at module top level then throws `volatile is not a function` at load time, which **takes the whole plugin down**. Detect first: ```js function supportsVolatile(S) { try { return typeof S.boolean().volatile === 'function' } catch { return false } } export const Config = supportsVolatile(Schema) ? Schema.object({ /* … */ }) : undefined ``` ## Self-check on any host Add a read-only self-check route that dumps these fields. When something is wrong, this one response tells you where: ```json { "ok": true, "value": { /* current settings value */ }, "revision": 1, "available": true, "probe": { "hasSettings": true, "hasDescribe": true, "count": 17, "ns": "agent-default-model,llm-pi-ai,…,ui-theme,locale,ui-settings,ui-conversation,…,ui-skin-claude-style", "namespaceState": "configured:ui-skin-claude-style", "error": null } } ``` Read it in this order: 1. Is your **bare id** in `probe.ns`? If not, it is trap 2 or trap 3. 2. Is `namespaceState` the **bare id**? A prefix like `include:` means trap 2. 3. Look at `hasSettings` and `hasDescribe`: does the host have this service at all? 0.1.5 does not, so take the legacy path. 4. Send `revision` on writes for optimistic concurrency. A mismatch returns `409 settings-conflict`, which is normal conflict semantics, not a bug. ## Compatibility recipe (one codebase, both versions) - Detect at startup. If the host has a settings service **and your bare id is in its list**, take the **0.1.7 path** and read and write by entry id. - Otherwise take the **0.1.5 legacy path**, with the plugin owning the namespace. - Both paths converge on the same in-memory "value + revision" model. The client only ever sees that one model, so "reads fine but cannot save" cannot happen. 0.1.7 also removed the old `scope.watch`. To follow changes, subscribe to the host's `settings/document-updated` event (its argument is the namespace id), or read the volatile `Config` field's `.get()` directly. You can also call `settings.configure({ auto: false }, ctx.fiber)` to declare "this plugin has its own settings page, do not generate a host page". That call returns a disposer, so register it with `ctx.effect(() => settings.configure(...))` instead of leaving the policy behind in the service. ## Also worth knowing (not the settings page, but hit in the same migration) - **The 0.1.7 plugin inventory reads `package.json` `icon`.** It must be a path relative to the manifest, inside the package, and no larger than 256 KiB. Absolute paths and URLs are rejected. Icons render as `` and **never receive `currentColor`**, so a dark icon disappears on the warm-black canvas. Prefer a coloured one. - **Localized metadata lives in `locale/.json` as `meta.title` and `meta.description`.** The host resolves it **file by file through the package `exports`**: if any single locale file is not exported, the **entire metadata, icon included, degrades to `meta.error`**. Use a wildcard `"./locale/*"` in `exports` instead of listing the files one by one. ## How this repository applies it `dsh-chat-import` has been migrated this way, with one codebase in `lib/import-prefs.mjs`: - `Config` is exported from the plugin entry (`lib/index.mjs`) with all three fields marked `.volatile()`. 0.1.7 only projects volatile fields into editable forms. - The namespace is the bare entry id. `entryIdOf()` strips the `:` prefix and falls back to the patch-declared `import-claude`. - Binding detection: if the `describe()` list contains the bare id, use `forms` (0.1.7); if only `register` and `get` exist, use `legacy` (0.1.5, namespace `chat-import`); if neither exists, use `none` (read defaults, writes are not persisted). - The panel route `/api-import/prefs` returns a `probe` self-check block.

# DSH 0.1.5 → 0.1.7 插件设置页迁移 [English](SETTINGS-MIGRATION.md) | 中文 本文整理了从 DSH 0.1.5 迁到 0.1.7 时踩到的全部设置页差异，每条都附实测报错的原文。可以直接 转发给其他插件作者。 ## 一句话 **0.1.7 删掉了 `settings.register()`。** 在 0.1.5 里，插件可以**按名字**给自己开一个设置 命名空间；到了 0.1.7，「命名空间就是 profile 里的一个条目 id，schema 就是那个条目的 Config」。 所以迁移不是改 API，而是**改这个插件在 profile 里的身份**。 ## 两版对照 | | 0.1.5 及更早 | 0.1.7 | |---|---|---| | 命名空间从哪来 | 插件自己 `settings.register('my-plugin', schema)` | profile 条目 id（[`cordis.patch.yml`](../cordis.patch.yml) 里那条 `- id: …`） | | schema 从哪来 | 注册时传进去 | 该条目的 `config` 字段，由宿主按插件的 `Config` 导出校验 | | 客户端怎么读写 | 走 api-proxy 暴露的 settings 通道 | 同上，但**命名空间必须在宿主那份名单里** | ## 三个坑（按踩到的顺序） ### 坑 1：`settings.register` 已经不是函数 **症状**出现在启动日志里。插件如果没兜住，会直接加载失败： ``` [modsearch] settings namespace skipped: TypeError: scope.settings.register is not a function ``` **修法**：别再调它。把 schema 作为插件的 `Config` 导出，客户端改用宿主的 settings 服务，按 **条目 id** 读写。 ### 坑 2：条目 id 带**种类前缀**，设置服务只认**裸 id** 这是最坑的一个。报错完全看不出真正的原因： ``` POST /my-plugin/prefs 409 settings-conflict No configurable plugin entry "include:ui-skin-claude-style" ``` **根因**：0.1.7 的 loader 把条目 id 报成 **`:`**。插件在 profile 里通常是 **`include` 或 `insert` 条目**，所以 `ctx.fiber.entry.id` 拿到的是 `include:ui-skin-claude-style`；而 **设置服务是按裸 id 给命名空间建索引的**，它的命名空间名单里写的就是 `ui-skin-claude-style`。 用带前缀的名字去写，宿主就找不到这个条目，于是**每次保存都 409**。 **修法**只要一行： ```js // 0.1.7 报的是 ":"，设置服务认的是裸 id；没有前缀时是无操作 function entryIdOf(ctx) { const id = ctx?.fiber?.entry?.id if (typeof id === 'string' && id !== '') { const colon = id.lastIndexOf(':') return colon === -1 ? id : id.slice(colon + 1) } return ENTRY_ID_FALLBACK // patch 里声明的那个 id } ``` **实测**：修前 `namespaceState = configured:include:ui-skin-claude-style`、写入 409；修后 `configured:ui-skin-claude-style`、写入 `200 {"ok":true,…,"revision":1,"available":true}`。 ### 坑 3：`schemastery` 从插件自己的位置解析不到 **症状**：Config 校验拿不到 schema，命名空间就注册不上。读能靠默认值兜住，但写一定失败。 **原因**：插件常常是以**软链或本地 link** 的方式装进 profile 的，它自己的 `require` 锚点下 根本没有 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`。 **修法**：把解析锚点指向**运行中的 harness bin**，它旁边一定带着 schemastery；失败再退回普通解析： ```js import { createRequire } from 'node:module' import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url' const anchor = pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href // 如 /@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js const factory = createRequire(anchor)('@deepseek-ai/schemastery') // 失败再 await import('@deepseek-ai/schemastery') ``` 还有一个坑是在**加载期**：`.volatile()` 是 0.1.7 才有的。旧宿主带的 schemastery 没有它，如果在 模块顶层直接构造带 volatile 的 `Config`，加载时就会抛 `volatile is not a function`，**整个插件 报废**。所以要先探测，再构造： ```js function supportsVolatile(S) { try { return typeof S.boolean().volatile === 'function' } catch { return false } } export const Config = supportsVolatile(Schema) ? Schema.object({ /* … */ }) : undefined ``` ## 怎么在任意宿主上自检 写一个只读的自检路由，把下面这几项吐出来。出问题的时候，光看这一个响应就能定位： ```json { "ok": true, "value": { /* 当前设置值 */ }, "revision": 1, "available": true, "probe": { "hasSettings": true, "hasDescribe": true, "count": 17, "ns": "agent-default-model,llm-pi-ai,…,ui-theme,locale,ui-settings,ui-conversation,…,ui-skin-claude-style", "namespaceState": "configured:ui-skin-claude-style", "error": null } } ``` 判读顺序： 1. 先看 `probe.ns` 里有没有你的**裸 id**。没有，就是坑 2 或坑 3。 2. 再看 `namespaceState` 里的是不是**裸 id**。带 `include:` 这类前缀，就是坑 2。 3. 看 `hasSettings` 与 `hasDescribe`：宿主到底有没有这套服务。0.1.5 没有，要走旧路径。 4. 写入时带上 `revision` 做乐观并发。不匹配会回 `409 settings-conflict`，这是正常的冲突语义，不是 bug。 ## 兼容写法（一套代码跑两版） - 启动时探测：宿主有 settings 服务，**并且你的裸 id 在名单里**，就走 **0.1.7 路径**，按条目 id 读写。 - 否则走 **0.1.5 旧路径**，由插件自持命名空间。 - 两条路径都收敛到同一个「值 + revision」的内存模型。客户端只认这一个模型，「读得出来、存不进去」就不会发生。 0.1.7 还移除了旧版的 `scope.watch`。要跟随设置变化，可以订阅宿主的 `settings/document-updated` 事件（参数是命名空间 id），也可以直接读 `Config` 里 volatile 字段的 `.get()`。另外可以调 `settings.configure({ auto: false }, ctx.fiber)`，声明「本插件自带设置页，不要生成宿主自动页」。 它返回一个 disposer，请用 `ctx.effect(() => settings.configure(...))` 登记，别把这段策略留在服务里。 ## 顺带（不是设置页，但同一次迁移里会撞到） - **0.1.7 的插件清单会读 `package.json` 的 `icon`**。它必须是相对清单的路径、留在包目录内、大小不超过 256 KiB；绝对路径和 URL 一律拒绝。图标按 `` 渲染，**拿不到 `currentColor`**，所以深色图标在暖黑画布上会消失，建议用有彩度的版本。 - **本地化元数据放在 `locale/<语言>.json` 的 `meta.title` 和 `meta.description`**。宿主是**逐个文件走包的 `exports`** 来解析的：只要有一个 locale 文件没被导出，**整份元数据（连同图标）都会降级成 `meta.error`**。所以 `exports` 里写通配 `"./locale/*"`，不要逐个文件列举。 ## 本仓库的落地 `dsh-chat-import` 已经按本文迁移完毕（`lib/import-prefs.mjs` 一套代码跑两版）： - `Config` 从插件入口（`lib/index.mjs`）导出，三个字段都标了 `.volatile()`（0.1.7 只把 volatile 字段投影成可编辑表单）。 - 命名空间就是裸条目 id。`entryIdOf()` 剥掉 `:` 前缀，剥完为空就回退到 patch 里声明的 `import-claude`。 - 绑定探测：`describe()` 的名单里含裸 id，走 `forms`（0.1.7）；只有 `register` / `get`，走 `legacy`（0.1.5，命名空间是 `chat-import`）；两者都没有，就是 `none`（读默认值，写入不持久化）。 - 面板路由 `/api-import/prefs` 的响应里带 `probe` 自检块。

# Usage Reference > Full per-tool / per-command usage moved out of the README. See the README "Usage" section for a quick start. ## 🛠 Usage > **First-migration step flow** (aligned with the [dsh-movein first-migration guide](https://github.com/sjh9714/dsh-movein/blob/main/docs/first-migration.zh.md), Chinese; that tool handles config, this plugin handles conversation history - use either standalone as needed): > ① **Preview** - `scan_discover()` or the sidebar panel to inspect importable sessions and status badges; or pass `preview: true` to `import_chat` for a zero-side-effect dry run. > ② **Import** - drop `preview` and import for real; verify the per-session `status` by source / workspace (duplicate-import behavior under "Incremental re-import" below). > ③ **Health check & retract** - `doctor()` read-only check; `retract_import` to remove the registry record, or the panel History tab to delete plugin-created sessions (with confirmation). > **Note:** imports persist to disk immediately. When the target generation equals the host's native generation (the panel's default), the new sessions appear in the session list immediately with no refresh; only an explicitly chosen non-native generation (e.g. producing a V3 log on a V4 host) is not the host's current in-memory shape and appears after a page refresh. ### For third-party plugins The plugin also registers an optional `chatImport` host service. Third-party plugins can call `scanDiscover()`, `importPath()`, `importAll()`, and `resumeSummary()` to reuse the same discovery, parsing, idempotency, compaction, batch-import, and handoff-summary pipelines as the built-in tools and commands. `importPath()` has the same result shape as `import_chat`: single-session imports include `sessionId`, while batch imports include `results`. Callers should degrade gracefully when the service is absent. ```js const service = ctx.get('chatImport') const found = await service.scanDiscover({ format: 'codex', query: 'fix' }) const selected = found.sessions[0] const imported = await service.importPath({ format: selected.format, path: selected.sourcePath, sessionIds: [selected.sessionId], }) const handoff = await service.resumeSummary({ format: selected.format, path: selected.sourcePath, sessionId: selected.sessionId, }) ``` `importAll()` accepts the same filters as `scanDiscover()` and returns batch counts, per-session results, and scan warnings. `resumeSummary()` currently supports Claude Code and Codex; it creates a handoff summary for injection into the current session and does not create or open a new DSH session. The caller opens an imported session with the returned `sessionId`. **Import — a single file or a directory.** One tool covers every source: `import_chat` takes a `format` and a `path`; directories are scanned recursively and each file / conversation becomes its own session: ``` import_chat({ format: "claude", path: "C:\Users\\.claude\projects\\.jsonl" }) import_chat({ format: "codex", path: "C:\Users\\.codex\sessions\2026\05\18\rollout-2026-05-18T21-14-16-xxxx.jsonl" }) import_chat({ format: "chatgpt", path: "C:\Users\\Downloads\chatgpt-export\conversations.json" }) import_chat({ format: "opencode", path: "C:\Users\\.local\share\opencode\opencode.db" }) import_chat({ format: "kilocode", path: "C:\Users\\.local\share\kilo\kilo.db" }) import_chat({ format: "teleagent", path: "C:\Users\\.local\share\TeleAgent\users\\teleagent.db" }) import_chat({ format: "trae", path: "C:\Users\\AppData\Roaming\Trae\User\workspaceStorage" }) import_chat({ format: "doubao", path: "C:\Users\\AppData\Local\Doubao\User Data" }) import_chat({ format: "vibe", path: "C:\Users\\.vibe\logs\session" }) import_chat({ format: "codearts", path: "C:\Users\\.codearts\kernel\sessions" }) import_chat({ format: "copilot-vscode", path: "C:\Users\\AppData\Roaming\Code\User\workspaceStorage" }) import_chat({ format: "copilot-cli", path: "C:\Users\\.copilot\session-state" }) import_chat({ format: "local-jsonl", path: "D:\downloads\session.jsonl" }) ``` `format: "local-jsonl"` accepts local session files (or a JSONL directory): it auto-detects `dsh` / `claude` / `codex` / `cursor` / `reasonix` / `pi` / `openclaw` / `hermes` / `qoder` / `vibe` / `codearts` / `codebuddy` / `generic` / `copilot-vscode` / `copilot-cli`, and the `parseFormat` parameter forces one parser when detection is wrong: ``` import_chat({ format: "local-jsonl", path: "D:\downloads\session.jsonl" }) import_chat({ format: "local-jsonl", path: "D:\downloads\unknown.jsonl", parseFormat: "claude" }) ``` `format: "chatgpt"` / `"opencode"` / `"kilocode"` / `"teleagent"` / `"trae"` / `"zcode"` / `"hermes"` (and the other one-database sources) always return a batch result — one file / database holds all conversations, so each conversation becomes its own session in a single call. opencode's `format` recognises its **two storage generations** and dispatches automatically: V1 (`session`/`message`/`part`) and V2 (opencode 2.x's `session_v2`/`session_message`) — both share the same `opencode.db`, where the V1 tables are only the V1→V2 migration source and survive it. Only the matched generation is read, so a session is never imported twice; a database with neither generation fails loudly instead of looking like "no sessions". `format: "teleagent"` also accepts the `users/` multi-account directory (it enumerates `/teleagent.db` per account) or the `TeleAgent/` data root directly. `format: "trae"` accepts a Trae `User` root, `workspaceStorage`, `globalStorage`, or a direct `state.vscdb` path. `format: "doubao"` accepts Doubao's `User Data` root, a profile directory, an `IndexedDB` directory, or a specific `chrome_doubao-chat_0.indexeddb.leveldb` database directory. Doubao keeps its conversation list server-side and caches bodies locally only for **recently opened** chats, so it lists and imports only conversations that actually have a locally cached body. Conversations without a cached body are neither listed nor importable (no shell session is fabricated from a title). When nothing is readable the import fails loudly with the database path and the count of undecodable records. `format: "copilot-vscode"` imports VS Code Copilot version 3 `chatSessions/*.json`: pass a `workspaceStorage` root, a `chatSessions` directory or a single JSON file. The panel discovers Code, Code - Insiders and VSCodium storage on Windows, macOS and Linux. `COPILOT_VSCODE_STORAGE_DIR` selects a portable storage root. Saved titles, source times, reasoning and tools are preserved. Tool parameters and results that VS Code did not save are counted as `missingToolInputs` and `missingToolOutputs`. See [IMPORT-GUIDE.md](IMPORT-GUIDE.md#copilot-vs-code). `format: "copilot-cli"` imports Copilot CLI session event streams (`~/.copilot/session-state//events.jsonl`): pass the `session-state` root, a session directory or a single `events.jsonl` file. `COPILOT_HOME` selects a moved `.copilot` root. Prompts, replies, reasoning and tool executions are replayed in order; source-side compactions become native DSH compaction checkpoints unless `fullHistory: true`. See [IMPORT-GUIDE.md](IMPORT-GUIDE.md#copilot-cli).
Import parameters & behaviors - `preview: true` (alias `dryRun: true`) — run the import **read-only**: resolve, read and convert exactly like a real import, but persist nothing (zero side effects). Drop the flag and call again to actually import. - **Kimi Code host injections no longer masquerade as user prompts, and parallel tool results keep their source order** — a new Kimi Code `context.append_message` carries `message.origin`: real input is `kind:"user"`, while date / permission / AGENTS.md / todo reminders, background-task completion notices and subagent events are `injection` / `task` / `system_trigger`. The converter used to open a user turn for every `role:"user"` record, so those tool notices and reminders showed up as user bubbles after import. They are now imported as `source.kind:"plugin"` context injections: the UI collapses them, their text and order are unchanged, and they do not count as messages or become the title fallback. Consecutive identical injections stay separate messages, and parallel tool results in one step are emitted in the source's completion order instead of being reordered to the call declaration order. Apart from DSH's own system head and environment-change notice, the imported history's message sequence matches the source transcript, and budget trimming keeps the opening anchor, so later requests do not get an additionally rewritten cache prefix because of the import. - **Images become host attachments** — images in the source no longer collapse to `[image]` text placeholders: the converter keeps the bytes in the intermediate structure, and before writing, the host attachment service (`ctx.attachments`) stores them as immutable objects while the session log keeps only an `attachmentId` reference (**base64 never reaches the log**). The result reports `images: ` (blocks stored as attachments) and `imagesDegraded: ` (blocks that had no bytes and stayed `[image]` placeholders: no attachment service on the host, unsupported media type (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF only), more than 500 images in one session, a source that only ships a reference such as Kimi's `blobref:`, or **a V3-generation target**). The export direction is symmetric: `export_chat({ format: "claude" })` / `export_chat({ format: "codex" })` read the bytes back into the target format and count `attachment-skipped` in `degradations` when they cannot. `storeImages: false` (or `DSH_IMPORT_STORE_IMAGES=0`) keeps placeholders only and writes nothing to the attachment store — images are the one import surface that can visibly grow host storage. **Deleting or retracting an imported session does not reclaim those image bytes**: the attachment service has no delete/GC API yet, so the objects stay in the store. - **Durations and token usage import faithfully** — per-record timestamps in the source become session event times, so host statistics fold real per-step model time and tool time (model time = step start → assistant message, tool time = call → result; sessions whose source has no per-record timestamps simply show 0, nothing is fabricated). Provider-reported token usage (Claude Code's `message.usage`, opencode / kilocode / mimocode's `message.data.tokens`, Reasonix v2 row-level `usage`) is written to `assistant/message.data.usage` for the host token meter; a record whose input/output is not a non-negative integer is dropped whole so statistics are never poisoned. Per-source support is the `timestamps` / `usage` columns of the capability matrix in [INTERCHANGE.md](INTERCHANGE.md). **Time-to-first-token and output speed cannot be imported from any source**: external transcripts only store completed messages, never stream-chunk times (`stream` stays `[]`). The opencode export direction is symmetric: events carrying usage fill `tokens` with real numbers, otherwise 0 is written and counted as `usage-unknown`. - `force: true` — create a **fresh full copy** under a new id (`import--`) even when the source was already imported; the old session is never modified (the full re-import policy is under "Re-importing the same source" below). - `sessionId` (optional) — override the target DSH session id (default `import-`). - `import_chat({ format: 'chatgpt', branch: 'all' })` — restore **every root→leaf branch** of the conversation DAG as its own session (the main thread stays the last-child chain; branch sessions carry a suffixed source id and a branch-marked title). Tool messages in the export are restored as real `tool/call` + `tool/result` (structured JSON arguments, FIFO pairing) instead of plain text. - **Context compaction → native DSH compaction events** — a source tool's compaction (Claude Code's `compact_boundary` / `isCompactSummary` user record and legacy `summary` records, Codex's `compacted` envelopes, Pi's `compaction` entries, opencode's `compaction` parts plus summary message (V2: the `compaction` row, checkpoint body = `summary` + `recent`), Kimi's `context.apply_compaction`, Zed's `Compaction` message, Crush's `is_summary_message`, Continue's `conversationSummary`, zcode's `compaction` part with `compactBoundary`, Cline's `.compaction.json` sidecar, Grok Build's `compaction_meta` hand-off summary, Mistral Vibe's `context_boundary = "compaction"`) is imported as a **native DSH compaction checkpoint**: the log keeps the **full history** (replayable, exportable) while one native `compaction/start → compaction/summary → checkpoint user/message → compaction/end` transaction is emitted per boundary. The model therefore sees "summary checkpoint + everything after the boundary", matching the source tool's real post-compaction context; the compacted-away conversation never reaches the model and is never eaten by budget trimming (shadowed turns are not counted, not cropped, not dropped). Several compactions produce several chained checkpoints. The result carries `compacted: true` and `compactions: ` (checkpoint count). **Re-importing a DSH session preserves the compaction transactions in its log** (`import_chat({ format: 'dsh' | 'dsh4' })` round-trips without losing checkpoints, normalizing the V3/V4 `plugin:compact` producer marker in both directions). When there is nothing shadowable before the boundary, or the source carries only a marker without summary text (Kimi's legacy wire), no checkpoint can be emitted — the summary falls back to its previous form (a reasoning block / visible text) or the case keeps the old window slice, and `compactionSummaryMissing: true` reports it explicitly instead of inventing summary text. `fullHistory: true` emits no checkpoints (the model sees everything); that flag is part of the args fingerprint, so changing it requires a re-import. oh-my-pi's `reset_boundary` (a `/clear` marker carrying no summary payload) follows the same rule as Kimi's summary-less wire: content before the last clear point does not enter the log and the result reports `resetBoundaries: `, while `fullHistory: true` keeps everything. - `import_chat({ format: 'claude', compacted: true })` — legacy flag kept as a compatible alias: Claude compaction is imported as native checkpoints **by default** as of this version, so the flag is no longer needed. - `import_chat({ format: 'claude', includeToolUseResult: true })` — additionally imports Claude's **structured tool result sidecar** (`toolUseResult`): edit patches (`structuredPatch` / `bashEditDiff`) become diff text, interactive questions/answers become Q&A pairs, and the remaining scalars (exit codes, durations, persisted output paths, …) become one compact JSON line — all appended after that tool result. Off by default (importing all of it grows the log noticeably); the flag is part of the argument fingerprint, so changing it requires `force`. The result reports `toolUseResultsMerged`, and whole-file snapshots (`originalFile`) plus anything already present in the visible body are never duplicated. - `import_chat({ format: 'codex', fullHistory: true })` — Codex compaction is imported as native checkpoints by default (the `compacted` envelope's hand-off summary becomes the checkpoint; the turn straddling the boundary is split into a log-only part and a visible part). `fullHistory: true` imports everything without checkpoints. Codex subagent rollouts are never standalone sessions and are always skipped with a reason. - **Codex compressed rollouts** — Codex 0.167+ stores finished sessions as `rollout-*.jsonl.zst`; only the few in-progress sessions stay plain `.jsonl`. The `codex` source discovers and imports both forms, decompressing `.zst` before conversion. When a page exists in both forms the newer file wins, and a rollout that later switches form keeps its existing import record, so archival never duplicates a session. - **Codex Desktop "import an external agent session" rollouts: flattened tool calls are restored as real tool messages** — when Codex Desktop's session import writes a foreign agent transcript (in practice Claude Code) into a rollout, …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… t); "Import selected" imports them one by one. **A failed detection is not a dead end**: the card leads with "Every conversation-format parser failed (N)", the **failure list starts collapsed** (press "Show failures (N)" for one "parser: reason" row each), and the line below says "Copy the failure summary to your agent" — what gets copied is a ready-to-send task brief (task statement + guide link + source path + output requirements + the per-parser failure reasons). The [interchange conversion guide](INTERCHANGE-GUIDE.md) itself (skill instructions for agents: the `"interchange": "dsh-chat-import"` marker, which any tool or script can produce) is also registered as the host runtime skill `dsh-chat-import-convert`, so an agent inside DSH can invoke it directly; the GitHub link is only a fallback. An unrecognised entry no longer shows all-zero turn/message/tool-call counts, nor repeats "unrecognized" — a file with 0 turns or no recognisable format disables the import button, and a blank, unopenable session is never produced. **Portable bundles**: a `.dshbundle.json` is recognised as a backup and imported through `restore_bundle` (two-layer fingerprint check, restored as a continuable session) instead of being treated as a plain transcript. **Upload staging**: chunked uploads are idempotent per (sha256, size) — a page refresh or a dropped connection resumes from the received byte count, and re-uploading the same file transfers nothing. A file only becomes importable after the whole-file fingerprint checks out. Limits: 256 MiB per file, 2 GiB of staging, incomplete uploads reclaimed after 24 hours. Imported staging files are **kept** (the re-import semantics key on them); unreferenced ones can be removed from the panel's staging-cleanup action. ### `/import` slash command & `/resume-*` handoff The plugin also registers a **`/import `** slash command (available where the dsh `commands` service is mounted): type it directly in a session to import without a model round-trip — the same pipeline and the same idempotent / incremental / `force` / context-budget semantics as the `import_chat` tool. `` accepts the short name (`claude`, `codex`, …), the client source id (`claude-code`), or the legacy tool-shaped alias (`import_claude`); `` is a transcript file or a session directory / data root (single-file import vs. directory batch as usual). **`/import-all [source] [path] [--force]`** scans the default data roots (or one source / explicit path) and imports every not-yet-imported session in one shot — same pipeline: skip when unchanged, append when untouched, new copy when you already chatted in the DSH session; archived and ignored sources skipped, and both failed scan targets and per-session failures are named. `--force` re-imports already-imported / archived sessions as fresh copies and **requires a `path` to bound the scope** (unbounded it would mint a copy of every imported session). The batch orchestration is the same function third-party plugins get as `chatImport.importAll` (`runChatImportAll` in `lib/chat-import-service.mjs`), so the two never drift on counting or failure reporting. **`/ignores`** lists the ignore table (auto-populated by archiving, deleting, and workspace removal); **`/ignore `** ignores one source manually; **`/unignore `** lifts entries (`all` clears the table). Ignored sources are skipped by rescans and `/import-all`; `force: true` imports once despite a tombstone without clearing it. **`/attach-workspaces`** re-attaches already-imported sessions to workspaces from the imports registry — useful for fixing early imports that landed in “未分组” / “Ungrouped”. It is idempotent and safe to re-run. Grouping is decided by **each session header's own cwd** (the host only accepts an attach whose cwd equals the workspace path): a cwd that already is a workspace attaches directly; a cwd that is a local directory gets a workspace created for it first; a cwd that is not on this machine (cross-machine import) or otherwise unusable is **reported as ungrouped** — a written session's cwd cannot be rewritten, so use `force: true` to re-import a copy that groups under the new landing point. Leave the argument empty for the most recent session, use `id:` for an exact one, or a title keyword — **multiple matches list candidates without guessing**: ``` /resume-claude id:282095ab-1111-4222-8333-444455556666 /resume-codex 修复登录 ``` ### Session-start context enhancements Two optional hooks run when a DSH session starts (the host `agent/session-start` event), both agent-scoped and never touching your transcripts: - **Migration hint (default on)** — when the session's workspace has discoverable external history (already-imported or importable), a one-line `PromptContext` is injected telling the model how to continue (`/import ` or the sidebar panel). The other 11 tools are the same trade in the "Full" mode.
